M1.Description: This category covers vulnerabilities resulting from hardcoding credentials, transmitting credentials in plaintext, or using weak authentication flows.
M1.Risk: Exposure of backend APIs, administrative dashboards, or other users' private data if hardcoded keys or credentials are leaked.
M1.Recommendation: Utilize secure credential management systems like Android Keystore, and never store plaintext keys in source/assets.

M2.Description: Vulnerabilities arising from third-party dependencies, malicious packages, or outdated SDKs loaded in the app.
M2.Risk: Possibility of remote code execution or data leakage through a compromised third-party library.
M2.Recommendation: Regularly audit third-party libraries and pin dependency versions to trusted releases.

M3.Description: Failures in verifying user identity or enforcing proper permissions on the client or server side.
M3.Risk: Bypassing authentication or accessing elevated administrative features without authorization.
M3.Recommendation: Implement server-side authentication validation and verify access tokens securely.

M4.Description: Failing to sanitize inputs from untrusted sources, potentially leading to SQL injection or script execution.
M4.Risk: Exploitation of internal SQLite databases or cross-site scripting in WebViews.
M4.Recommendation: Use parameterized queries and validate all input sources (Intents, files, inputs).

M5.Description: Transmission of sensitive data over unencrypted (HTTP) or weakly encrypted channels.
M5.Risk: Man-in-the-Middle (MitM) attacks leading to intercepting active session tokens or credentials.
M5.Recommendation: Enforce SSL/TLS for all connections, declare cleartextTrafficPermitted as false, and implement certificate pinning.

M6.Description: Accidental exposure of PII (Personally Identifiable Information) or sensitive user metrics to analytics or logging.
M6.Risk: Legal/regulatory non-compliance (e.g. GDPR) and violation of user privacy.
M6.Recommendation: Minimize PII storage and encrypt any data tracked for analysis or reporting.

M7.Description: Lack of code obfuscation, integrity checks, or anti-debug guards, enabling easy reverse engineering.
M7.Risk: Attackers decompiling the application, discovering proprietary algorithms, and rewriting application logic.
M7.Recommendation: Enable ProGuard/R8 obfuscation and incorporate anti-debugging/anti-tampering library components.

M8.Category: M8: Security Decisions via Untrusted Inputs
M8.Description: Using weak client-side checks or spoofable Intent data to make critical access control decisions.
M8.Risk: Unauthorized access to application features through forged IPC signals or Intents.
M8.Recommendation: Perform critical security state checks on a secure backend server.

M9.Description: Storing sensitive information in unprotected files, databases, or preferences on the local filesystem.
M9.Risk: Malicious applications or root users reading private data directly from the device storage.
M9.Recommendation: Store private data in internal directories and encrypt SQLite database backups.

M10.Description: Use of obsolete or weak cryptographic algorithms (MD5, SHA1, DES) or poor key management.
M10.Risk: Fast decryption of intercepted data or compromised storage because of weak key design.
M10.Recommendation: Implement industry-standard cryptography protocols like AES-GCM and RSA-OAEP.
